cards.explanation: The answer is things visible and invisible. Paul says all things were created in the Son, "…things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible…" (Colossians 1:16). That covers what you can see and what you can't. I once spent years in the dark of a junk drawer, and even there, nothing was outside what He made.

The answer is False. Paul lists thrones, dominions, rulers and authorities, and then says "All things were created through Him and for Him." (Colossians 1:16). Not one of those powers was made apart from Him. Big titles, same Maker, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says the Son "…is before all things, and in Him all things hold together." (Colossians 1:17). Both halves are in the same verse. The Son comes first, and in Him all things hold together.

The answer is so He has first place in all things. Paul says it's "…so that in all things He may have preeminence." (Colossians 1:18). Preeminence means first place. The Son is the head of the body, the beginning, the firstborn from among the dead, and Paul ties all of that to this one purpose.
The answer is False. Paul says "…God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him…" (Colossians 1:19). The word is ALL, friends. Nothing is left out.

The answer is through the blood of His cross. Paul says God reconciles all things to Himself "…by making peace through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). The peace comes through the cross. Paul says it plainly, and I never get tired of hearing it.

The answer is False. Paul says "Once you were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds." (Colossians 1:21). Alienated means far away, not close. Paul is honest about where they started.

The answer is True. Paul says "…He has reconciled you by Christ’s physical body through death to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence…" (Colossians 1:22). Three words, and each one is good news. Paul says it, so I'll say it loud.

The answer is the hope of the gospel they heard. Paul says to continue "…established and firm, not moved from the hope of the gospel you heard…" (Colossians 1:23). Stay put, friends, because a stamper who stays pressed down makes a clean cookie.

The answer is its servant. Paul says the gospel "…has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and of which I, Paul, have become a servant." (Colossians 1:23). Paul is a servant, and he says so himself. I think that's a humble way to put it.
